prompt_source: Ch9 three-email sequence brief (lines 1644-1652), with Ch7 sample kit plus <offer>/<proof>

turns.prompt:
<bio>
Maya Torres is a career coach for mid-career nurses who want to move
into healthcare leadership without leaving patient care behind. After
14 years as an ICU nurse and four as a nurse manager, she started her
practice in 2023. She is known for practical, no-nonsense sessions and
a habit of asking "What would you tell a new grad in your shoes?"
</bio>

<audience>
Registered nurses, 8 to 20 years in, mostly women in their late 30s to
40s. Respected on their units, often the informal charge nurse, but
passed over or unsure about formal leadership. Fear: becoming "a
suit" who forgets the floor. Desire: influence over how care is
delivered. Phrases they use (from client intake forms): "I'm already
doing the job, just without the title." "I don't want to sell out."
Inference, unconfirmed: many are the main earner in their household.
</audience>

<message>
You do not have to choose between leading and caring. The best nurse
leaders lead because they care, and the skills that make you good at
the bedside are most of what leadership needs.
</message>

<voice>
1. Short sentences. 2. Starts with a scene from a shift. 3. Uses
nursing language naturally, never explains it. 4. Warm but blunt.
5. No exclamation marks. 6. One question to the reader per piece,
near the end. 7. Never uses "self-care" or "empower." 8. Humor is
dry and about hospital life. 9. Ends with a concrete next step.
10. Signs off "Maya."
</voice>

<offer>
Charge to Chair: a six-week online leadership program for RNs with 8+ years of experience. Six live Tuesday-evening Zoom sessions (7 to 8:30 p.m. Pacific), weekly worksheets, and one 30-minute 1:1 call with Maya. Price $690, or 3 payments of $240. Cohort limited to 20 seats so every 1:1 call fits in Maya's calendar. Starts November 17, 2026.
</offer>

<proof>
"I went from informal charge nurse to unit educator in four months, and I still work two bedside shifts a month." Dana R., RN, ICU, pilot cohort 2025 (shared with permission).
</proof>

Write a three-email sequence for the program in <offer>, using my kit.
Email 1 (problem aware): the "already doing the job" frustration; no
pitch; ends with a question to reply to.
Email 2: why generic leadership training does not fit nurses; introduce
the program; one real testimonial from <proof>.
Email 3: the offer, the real enrollment deadline of November 10, 2026, and the
three most common objections answered.
Each under 250 words. Subject line plus preview text for each. Use
only facts in <offer> and <proof>. Write [NEED] where proof is missing.
turns.output:
Email 1
Subject: You're already doing the job
Preview: Just without the title, the differential, or a say in staffing.

It's 3 a.m. The board looks like a lost-and-found. You float the post-op, catch the missed insulin, and still take the rapid.

Nobody wrote charge next to your name. They still look at you when the census tips.

You are already doing the job. Just without the title, the differential, or a vote when they rewrite the staffing grid.

They will keep handing you the hard admits. Then they will promote the person who left at 1900 with a clean assignment.

That is not being a team player. That is extra labor in ugly Crocs.

You did not stay this long to remain unofficial forever.

Where are you already leading without the title?

Hit reply and tell me.

Maya.

Email 2
Subject: Leadership class was not built for nurses
Preview: Stakeholders and synergy. No mention of the board or hanging blood.

The consultant stands in huddle with a clicker. She says stakeholder buy-in. Half your staff is still in report. The other half is hanging blood.

Generic leadership training was built for people who leave at 1700 and call that late.

It has never seen a nurse who is informal charge, precepting, and covering the crash cart because biomed is aware.

You do not need another module on synergy. You need to lead without turning into a suit who forgets the floor.

The best nurse leaders lead because they care. The skills that make you good at the bedside are most of what leadership needs.

That is why I built Charge to Chair. Six weeks, for RNs with 8+ years. Six live Tuesday-evening Zoom sessions, 7 to 8:30 p.m. Pacific. Weekly worksheets. One 30-minute 1:1 call with me.

Dana R., RN, ICU, pilot cohort 2025: "I went from informal charge nurse to unit educator in four months, and I still work two bedside shifts a month."

What did the last leadership in-service get wrong for your unit?

Hit reply.

Maya.

Email 3
Subject: Charge to Chair closes November 10
Preview: 20 seats. Starts November 17. $690 or three payments of $240.

You are in the med room counting. Days pokes in. Can you just cover charge again. It will be easy. It is never easy.

Charge to Chair is a six-week online leadership program for RNs with 8+ years. Six live Tuesday-evening Zoom sessions, 7 to 8:30 p.m. Pacific. Weekly worksheets. One 30-minute 1:1 call with me. Cohort limited to 20 seats so every 1:1 call fits in my calendar. Starts November 17, 2026. Enrollment closes November 10, 2026.

Price is $690, or 3 payments of $240.

I do not have time. This is six Tuesday nights plus worksheets. You already stay late to fix the board.

I do not want to sell out. You do not have to choose between leading and caring. Dana R., RN, ICU, went from informal charge nurse to unit educator in four months, and still works two bedside shifts a month.

Six hundred ninety dollars is a lot. That is the price. Three payments of $240 is the other option.

Will you take one of the 20 seats, or stay unnamed charge through another winter?

Enroll here: [NEED]

Maya.
